slides.texte_overlay:
unusual hobbies that make
you wildly intelligent

reading old letters

read the published letters of famous people. private letters show how great minds really thought, doubted and argued, far better than any textbook can.

naming the clouds

learn the names of ten types of cloud and look for them on your walks. it trains your attention, and the sky suddenly becomes something worth reading.

one lesson a day

i used to only study my own subject. a short daily lesson on everything else, from art to history to science, completely changed the way i think and connect ideas.
slides.texte_sophia:
one lesson a day

i used to only study my own subject. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app, art, history, science, and i make connections i never saw before.

slides.texte_overlay:
translating songs

translate the lyrics of a song in a language you don't speak. you learn words, grammar and a little culture at once, and the song suddenly means so much more.

memory walks

before sleep, walk through your home in your head and place every object. it sounds strange, but it's one of the oldest and best ways to train your memory.
